title: AlderStream fleet onramp ramble
content:
Context:
- AlderStream: regional logistics operator (light trucks, ~650 vehicles). Looking to add an LLM-driven ETA and driver-assist layer to routing dashboard.
- Use case: live ETA corrections, short-turn routing suggestions, natural-language exception explanations for dispatchers.
- Primary constraint: many edge sites (depots) have flaky cellular; some vehicles send short telemetry bursts only.
- Security: customer requires VPC + customer-managed KMS for any PII/vehicle id persistence.
- Legal/regulatory: driver logs considered personal data in EU regions -> retention & redaction rules must be enforced.

Call notes (2025-11-03 kickoff, 45m):
- Intro: AlderStream ops and platform team (Tom H., Leila) and product manager (Anita). They want rapid prototype with host + private combo.
- Goals they stated: reduce dispatch calls by 15% (explanations), reduce late arrivals >5min by 20% in 90 days.
- Throughput: expect ~1200 requests/min during peak (regional), each request small (prompt + ~80 tokens expected).
- SLO: 95th latency <200ms for quick suggestions; possible to relax for full explanations (500-800ms).
- Data flow preference: telemetry + route snapshot posted to Redwood endpoint; customer prefers ephemeral-only storage and no long-term logs in hosted plane.
- Compliance ask: ability to redact VIN/driver_id server-side before any tokens hit hosted models; also must support local redaction step in Private runtime.
- On-prem note: two depots considering Dedicated capacity (Nvidia T4 pools) for heavy daytime throughput and occasional on-prem gateway for failover.
- Observability: they want per-driver cost breakdown and token-level latency traces.

Immediate technical requirements (draft):
- VPC peering + Private deployment has to support SAML SSO + KMS integration (customer KMS: HashiCorp Vault).
- Redaction middleware: must run inside customer's network or pre-processing lambda to scrub VIN/driver_id/phone before sending prompt.
- Model variants: need a small, quantized 7B-ish fallback locally (for latency) and a larger 13B hosted for richer explanations.
- Streaming: must support chunked streaming so dispatch UI can show incremental suggestion tokens (reduces perceived latency).
- Caching: prefix caching for repeated route fragments to cut cost; cache keyed by route-hash + vehicle-history-hash.
- Burst capacity and autoscale: Dedicated pool should autoscale on day-start spikes (6am PST) and allow short burst to hosted if Dedicated is saturated.

Gotchas / open risks noted:
- Telemetry bursts: intermittent telemetry means model must gracefully handle partial context — design prompt templates to include confidence meta or fall back to last-known-location heuristics.
- Redaction leakage: risk that identifiers embedded in telemetry text fields might bypass simple regexes (e.g., VIN encoded inside gps telemetry tags). Need layered redaction + allow customer to supply field whitelist.
- Token accounting: dispatch UI will run many quick suggestions; must watch unit cost as high-frequency short calls can be expensive without batching/prefetch.
- Edge network cost: Private runtime at depots may still rely on hosted model for richer outputs — must plan egress patterns and cold-starts for fallback models.
- Driver safety: suggestions must never encourage unsafe maneuvers. Need explicit safety filter and rule-based blockers before surfaced suggestions.

Prototype plan (two-week sprint sketch):
Week 0 (prep):
- Internal: map & size interfaces, produce sample telemetry -> prompt templates (Priya + Liam).
- AES: share minimal SSO + KMS integration checklist with AlderStream security (Sofia).
Week 1:
- Build redaction middleware (edge lambda) + sample harness to replay telemetry to sandbox.
- Spin up Dedicated T4 pool in staging, deploy quantized 7B fallback model, test latency.
- Create initial prompt set for ETA corrections + explanation style guidelines.
Week 2:
- Integrate streaming response to dispatch UI mock (front-end stub).
- Run small closed pilot with 25 vehicles for 48h (measure latency, token counts, failure modes).
- Collect evals: percent of useful suggestions (ops-labelled), false-safety triggers.

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Priya: draft prompt templates + sample telemetry schema (due 2025-11-06).
- Liam: spike Dedicated T4 runner + quantize baseline model; record perf matrix (due 2025-11-08).
- Sofia: security checklist + Vault KMS integration steps; confirm SAML mapping with AlderStream (due 2025-11-07).
- Ethan: build redaction lambda prototype (configurable field whitelist + regex + entropy checks) and run on sample traces (due 2025-11-06).
- Tom H. (AlderStream): provide anonymized telemetry dump (25 vehicles, 24h) and list of fields that cannot leave their network (due 2025-11-05).

Design decisions to confirm with product/legal:
- Retention policy: Hosted plane must not persist raw telemetry — only aggregated metrics allowed. Confirm deletion window (24h? 7d?).
- Redaction guarantee level: do we require formal proof-of-redaction (hash fingerprinting) or is 'best-effort' acceptable for pilot?
- Safety policy thresholds: who signs off on rule-based blockers for driver safety? ops or legal?

Notes-to-self / rough ideas:
- Consider model priming with a short, structured JSON response schema (action:{type,score,reasons[]}) so UI can render decisions reliably.
- Use prefix-KV cache for common route segments (inter-city connectors) to get sub-100ms hits for simple rewrites.
- Explore tiny rule-based edge model for safety checks to avoid roundtrip to hosted model for obvious unsafe suggestions.
- Cost optimization: batch multiple vehicle peek-requests within 100ms windows where possible to leverage continuous batching in runtime.

Unresolved questions:
- AlderStream wants token-level cost per-driver — can we expose that without leaking cross-driver details? (product/privacy tradeoff)
- Do they need offline evaluation harness (yes likely) — set up Confluence eval page and shared S3 for labels.
- Deployment: will they accept containerized Private runtime or prefer fully managed appliance?

Quick links / references:
- internal: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Private+deployment+patterns
- benchmark notes: RED-OPS-llm-latency-2025 (internal doc id)

Status: rough prototype plan defined; waiting on telemetry dump + security signoff.

End of scratchpad.
